title: Climb the ladder
scenario: You climb a ladder taking 1 or 2 rungs at a time. How many different ways can you climb 6 rungs?

intro.job: You climb a ladder taking 1 or 2 rungs at a time. How many different ways can you climb 6 rungs?

idea.rule: Each step comes from the two BEFORE it — update both from the old values at once.
idea.detail: To reach rung i, your last move was either a 1-rung hop (from i - 1) or a 2-rung hop (from i - 2) — so ways(i) = ways(i - 1) + ways(i - 2). Instead of recursing, roll forward: keep just the last two answers, a and b, and move them up one rung at a time — both from the values they held before the pass, so each rung is built from the two before it. Each pass of the loop climbs one rung, so it has to run all the way up to and including rung n.

watch.code:
a = 1
b = 1
for i in range(2, n + 1):
    a, b = b, a + b
answer = b
print(answer)

model_restatement: Count the different sequences of 1-rung and 2-rung hops that add up to n.

clarify.question: Can I hop 3 rungs at once?
Does order matter?
clarify.answer: Yes — 1 then 2 is a different way from 2 then 1.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Rungs 0 and 1 have 1 way each. For each rung from 2 up to n, the ways are the two before it added. Print the ways for n.
draft_code:
a = 1
b = 1
for i in range(2, n + 1):
    b = a + b
    a = b
answer = b
print(answer)

checkpoints.prompt: Iteration 2 (rung 3): after line 4, what is b?
The loop is done. What is answer?
With the fix — when the loop is done, what is answer?

why_line: b = a + b then a = b updates one at a time — b is already new when a copies it, so each pass doubles b: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, not 2, 3, 5, 8, 13.

explain.rule: Each step comes from the two BEFORE it — update both from the old values at once.
explain.bridge: After rung 3, b should be 3 — the ways for rungs 1 and 2 added. What is b after the second pass, and which line made it that?

fix.rule: a, b = b, a + b: both update from the OLD values at once, so each rung is built from the two before it.

walk.gloss: Ways to stand on rung 0 (doing nothing).
Climb rung 2, 3, … all the way to n.
Both change at once from the old values — new b is old a + old b, and a takes old b.

contrast.wrong_note: b is already new when a copies it — each rung doubles
contrast.right_note: both read the old values, so each rung adds the two before it

fix.recommended:
a = 1
b = 1
for i in range(2, n + 1):
    a, b = b, a + b
answer = b
print(answer)

alternatives.note: Count the ways by splitting on the first hop — correct, but it re-counts the same rungs again and again.

hints: After rung 3, what should b be — and what is it?
The second line copies b after b already changed.
